title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS2 likely contains unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs, session IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different sessions and contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location data
description: Location history data contains combinations of attributes (timestamps, locations, routes) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Profiling an individual through location patterns
description: The Health Analytics Service derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history, which constitutes profiling an individual based on their behavioral data and location patterns.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The data flow involves processing of identified location history data that can be directly associated with specific data subjects.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes (home location, workplace, frequent destinations) that support identification of the data subject's identity and lifestyle.

title: Sensitive location data type collected
description: Location history is considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations, and its collection may exceed what is strictly required for the stated functionality.

title: Excessive analysis and pattern derivation
description: The analytics service performs additional processing (deriving daily routines and movement patterns) that may not be strictly necessary for the core functionality of the system.

title: Unawareness of location history processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried and analyzed across sessions to derive behavioral patterns.

title: Lack of control over location data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location history is processed and what patterns are derived from it.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history across multiple sessions to derive detailed movement patterns may process more personal data than is actually needed for the stated functionality.

title: Profiling individual through inferred health conditions
description: The app analyzes user data to infer eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, creating profiles that link data to specific individuals through pattern analysis.
assumptions: The app has access to sufficient historical health data to perform meaningful inference

title: Quasi-identifier combination through health indicators
description: Health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) combined with other user attributes could serve as quasi-identifiers that link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Health indicators are combined with other user data that could be used for re-identification

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed to user
description: The dashboard displays revealing health attributes (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) that could support identification of the data subject when combined with other information.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are personally identifiable when viewed in context

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The system processes identified health data to generate and display condition indicators to the user.
assumptions: User data is linked to identifiable individuals before processing

title: Sensitive health data type disclosure
description: The app displays highly sensitive health data (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) which may be more sensitive than functionally required for the dashboard display.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: The app performs analysis and enrichment of health data to create risk signals, which may exceed what is functionally needed for basic dashboard display.
assumptions: The inference/analysis process adds value beyond simple data display

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data is being analyzed to generate risk indicators displayed on the dashboard.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain the inference mechanisms

title: Lack of user control over health data processing
description: Users may lack control over preferences regarding how their health data is processed and what risk indicators are displayed.
assumptions: Limited user customization options for data processing preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The app processes health data to generate risk signals that may exceed what is functionally needed for the dashboard functionality.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires processing only necessary data

title: Automated decision making on sensitive personal data
description: The app uses automated analysis to generate health risk signals (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) which may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are considered sensitive personal data requiring special protection
